claims.value: Building B: 188 rental units, 100% affordable for low-income seniors; Building A: 253 market-rate rental units

City BMR requirement for Building A (253 market-rate units) is 38 lower-income rental units. Under an Applicant-Proposed Alternative (BMR Guidelines Sec. VIII(d)) the requirement is met in Building B, where all 188 units would be deed-restricted affordable rentals for low-income seniors

claims.note: Application filed under SB 330 and the State Density Bonus Law
Project number on the city project page; the development list and the 2026-10-05 Council agenda report use PA-2026-0025

construction_notes.text: Two eight-story buildings, about 95 feet tall; Building A has a podium-top pool deck and two courtyards
Replaces an existing five-story office building (Borel Estate Building)

The October 5, 2026 Council agenda report states the applicant does not plan to use City or County funds and plans to use private activity tax-exempt bonds for the affordable senior building (Building B).

The agenda report lists the planning application as a Site Plan and Architectural Review, Site Development Planning Application and Vesting Tentative Map; site designated Mixed-Use High (up to eight stories, 130 units/acre). CEQA review under Guidelines Section 15183; Planning Commission hearing anticipated toward the end of 2026.
Proposed condition: Building A (market-rate) would not receive a certificate of occupancy until Building B (affordable) has a building permit and has started construction.

Building B unit counts differ by source: the city project page lists 186 units plus 2 manager units, with 150 one-bedroom and 38 two-bedroom; the Council agenda report lists 188 units with 150 one-bedroom and 28 two-bedroom.

events.label: City Council considers resolution approving alternative BMR compliance (Building B senior affordable units)
